catalog_quote: Finally, stress in Ende falls on the penultimate syllable, unless the penultimate syllable contains a schwa. In that case, stress falls on the ultimate syllable. Stress is usually marked by an increase in intensity and vowel length. ... [p. 208] the mid-central vowel is phonetically shorter than all other vowels and never takes stress or prominence in the root or the word. ... Lastly, the schwa is limited to the first syllable of bisyllabic words as well as the numeral proclitic sa /sə/ and the prepositional proclitic pa /pə/; that is, it is disallowed in the ultimate syllable. ... [p. 211] The defining characteristics of clitics in Ende are: 1) clitics are one only syllable, 2) clitics have a phonetically short vowel, and 3) clitics are always unstressed. ... audit.reasoning: Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation (stress rule p. 211, schwa never stressed / barred from the ultima p. 208, clitics always unstressed p. 211, wordlist items 206-215 p. 224) is verbatim in the held JSEALS-2 text at the cited pages. The coding (right-edge penult default, final stress when the penult is schwa; class full-vs-reduced-vowel; no secondary stress described; domain WORD with clitics excluded) follows the source exactly, and the transcribed wordlist independently shows the pattern ([təˈɹu], [səmˈbuɹu] vs [ˈßutu], [səˈŋasu]). Deciding source is a 2009 peer-reviewed phonology article from primary fieldwork and is the sole descriptive reference Glottolog holds for this languoid; no grammar, dissertation or instrumental study of Flores Ende stress was found.
